{{Top}}
{{MultipleIssues|expand|image}}
{{Quote|Nothing is impossible with the Force.|[[Kreia]]|<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref>}}
[[File:The_Force.png|thumb|right|250px|[[Anakin Skywalker|Anakin]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] use [[Telekinesis/Legends#Force Push|Force push]] against each other.]]

'''Force powers''' were the manifestations of a [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] being's connection with [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], an energy field that surrounded and bound together everything in existence. The nature and practice of such abilities were usually taught to learners by experienced practitioners, such as the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] and the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]]. Some techniques required a deep connection with either the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light side]] or the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] of the Force, but many were not specific to either affinity. The Force was practiced as a form of magic by some groups, such as the [[Witches of Dathomir]], [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsisters]], [[Mind-witch]]es, and users of [[Sith sorcery/Legends|Sith magic]] and [[Sith alchemy/Legends|Sith alchemy]]. Force powers can also be used to levitate objects, calm animals, and sense others' feelings.

==Description==
===Overview===
The Force expressed itself as the [[Living Force/Legends|Living Force]] and the [[Unifying Force/Legends|Unifying Force]]. While the Unifying Force was vast and cosmic, part of space and time rather than physical bodies, the Living Force was close to beings in their lives and [[Death/Legends|deaths]]. Tangible Force abilities&mdash;such as soothing others' emotions, moving objects, heightening the senses, jumping, and running&mdash;were techniques related to the Living Force.<ref name="The Jedi Path">[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'']]</ref>

===The Jedi Order===
{{Quote|A Jedi uses the Force for knowledge and defense, never for attack.|Former [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]]|<ref name="Episode 5">{{Film|V}}</ref>}}
[[File:Jedi_symbol.svg|thumb|right|200px|A symbol of the Jedi Order]]
The [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] classified abilities with [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] according to three themes: [[Control]], [[Sense]], and [[Alter (Jedi Order)|Alter]]. [[Jedi Initiate/Legends|Jedi Initiates]] studied Control, which was centered in one's own body and regarded as the basic skills used throughout a being's lifetime. [[Padawan/Legends|Padawans]] progressed to Sense, extending themselves into their surrounding environment and expanding their awareness of the Living Force. As [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]], their education was furthered with Alter, the abilities that physically impacted their surroundings and were the most difficult to master.<ref name="The Jedi Path" />

===The Sith===
{{Quote|A Sith knows when to unleash the fury of the dark side, and when to hold back. Patience can be a weapon if you know how to use it, and your anger can fuel the dark side if you learn how to control it.|Darth Bane|<ref name="Darth Bane: Rule of Two">''[[Darth Bane: Rule of Two]]''</ref>}}
<span class="invert-images">[[File:Sith_Emblem.svg|thumb|left|200x|An emblem of the Sith]]</span>
The [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith Purebloods]] developed ritual methods of manipulating the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]] through incantations and gestures; the techniques were later adopted by the [[Exiles|exiled]] [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] on [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]] and the [[Order of the Sith Lords]]. A [[Sith sorcerer]]'s [[Sith sorcery/Legends|spellcasting]] techniques could be enhanced by the use of specific amulets or raiments.<ref name="Book of Sith">''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''</ref>

The [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] of [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane's]] legacy divided their powers into three schools or focuses that channeled the dark side: [[Offense]], [[Body]], and [[Mind]]. Offense included skills that were dynamic, immediately applicable to [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|lightsaber combat]], and required relatively little exertion to deploy. Body drew upon the Living Force in one's own cells to affect another's on the physical plane; as such, it could damage one's body and be hindered by the presence of [[Cybernetics/Legends|cybernetics]]. Mind, which drew upon the Unifying Force, operated in memory and thought rather than the body or physical strength; its disciplines demanded intense concentration and psychic clarity.<ref name="Book of Sith" />

==Applications==
===By the Jedi Order===
====Control====
{{Main|Control}}
{{Quote|Control is internal. It is the Jedi's ability to recognize the Force in himself and to use it to his benefit.|[[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Bodo Baas]]|<ref name="Jedi vs. Sith">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref>}}
[[File:CenterofBeing.jpg|thumb|right|200px|A Jedi [[Center of Being|centers himself]] in preparation for combat.]]
The Jedi Order's teaching method began with the aspect of Control, taught to Jedi Initiates as a way to open their minds to the Force and establish a base point for further development. Control was centered on the Initiate's own body and self. Development of these skills would continue throughout a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi's]] life and serve as the foundation for subsequent disciplines.<ref name="The Jedi Path" />

Three main abilities were centered around Control: ''[[tutaminis]]'' (energy absorption), ''[[curato salva]]'' (healing one's own self), and ''[[altus sopor]]'' (increasing one's focus on the Force).<ref name="The Jedi Path" />

====Sense====
{{Main|Sense}}
{{Quote|&hellip;Sense involves the next step, in which the Jedi recognizes the Force in the universe outside herself.|Jedi Master Bodo Baas|<ref name="Jedi vs. Sith" />}}
The Sense discipline was taught to Padawans to broaden the scope of their Control abilities. Dipping into a deeper understanding of the Living Force, Sense abilities allowed Force-wielders to immerse themselves in the environment. By the end of their apprenticeship, Padawans were expected to use the Force as an additional sense and be constantly attuned to its undulations.<ref name="The Jedi Path" />

The Jedi Order divided Sense abilities into four main groups: [[Life Detection|''prima vitae'']] (life detection), [[Sense Force|''tactus otium'']] (Sense Force), [[Psychometry/Legends|''tai vordrax'']] (postcognition), and [[Telepathy/Legends|projected telepathy]]. While there were many other styles to the Sense family, these were considered the most vital to Jedi teachings.<ref name="The Jedi Path" />

====Alter====
{{Main|Alter (Jedi Order)}}
{{Quote|Alter is the third and most difficult area to master, for it involves the student's ability to modify the Force and redistribute its energies.|Jedi Master Bodo Baas|<ref name="Jedi vs. Sith" />}}
[[File:YodaForceLift.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Yoda using telekinesis to lift [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker's]] [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing]].]]
The Jedi Order regarded the Alter discipline as an advanced form of Force use, taught to Jedi Knights who had mastered the arts of Control and Sense. It involved manipulating objects, influencing other beings, and affecting the environment. Such abilities needed to be perfected and honed, but many non-trained Force-sensitives stumbled upon such powers accidentally, which usually resulted in disastrous events. Without advancing to the Alter discipline, individuals could see the Force, but were incapable of manipulating it.<ref name="The Jedi Path" />

The fundamental Alter techniques were: [[Telekinesis/Legends|telekinesis]], [[Mind trick/Legends|affect mind]], and [[Alter Environment]].<ref name="The Jedi Path" />

====Jedi career paths====
Jedi Knights and [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]] pursued different careers within the Order based on their innate abilities, including their use of Force powers.<ref name="The Jedi Path" /> [[Jedi Consular]]s emphasized the more cerebral Force skills<ref name="KOTOR 4">[[Knights of the Old Republic 4|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 4]]</ref> and tended to utilize those powers rather than their [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]]. [[Precognition/Legends|Precognition]] and postcognition, [[Force healing/Legends|healing]], and strong empathic talents were among their specialties. [[Jedi Guardian/Legends|Jedi Guardians]] often used the Force to enhance their physical capabilities, such as their reaction speed and battle awareness, but they were better known for their talents with lightsabers. [[Jedi Sentinel/Legends|Jedi Sentinels]], as described by [[Jedi recruiter]] [[Morrit Ch'gally/Legends|Morrit Ch'gally]], struck a balance between the Guardians and the Consulars and also developed more practical abilities that did not rely upon the Force; however, some had an intuitive understanding of machinery and technology through ''[[mechu-deru]]''.<ref name="The Jedi Path" />

===By the Sith===
====Offense====
{{Main|Offense}}
{{Quote|Offense encompasses the Force skills with immediate, dynamic applications for lightsaber combat.|Darth Bane, in ''Book of Sith''|<ref name="Book of Sith" />}}
In Darth Bane's teachings, the school or focus called Offense included immediately applicable techniques that required little exertion, making them particularly useful in lightsaber duels. Such skills included [[Inertia]], [[Force blinding|Blind]], Push, Choke, and Throw.<ref name="Book of Sith" />

====Body====
{{Main|Body}}
{{Quote|The second school, or focus, Body, encompasses those abilities that draw from the living Force. They emanate from your own cells and affect the physical structures of others.|Darth Bane, in ''Book of Sith''|<ref name="Book of Sith" />}}
Another of Bane's teachings, Body drew from the living Force in one's own cells to physically affect another being, at the possible cost of damaging the user's own body. Body techniques included [[Force lightning/Legends|lightning]], [[convection]], [[cryokinesis]], [[Force drain/Legends|drain life]], and death field.<ref name="Book of Sith" />

====Mind====
{{Main|Mind}}
{{Quote|The third school, or focus, Mind, encompasses those abilities that draw from the unifying Force. These operate on a different plane than the physical&mdash;they exist in the realm of thought and memory.|Darth Bane, in ''Book of Sith''|<ref name="Book of Sith" />}}
The last of Bane's focuses or schools was Mind, drawing upon the unifying Force to act upon thought and memory instead of the physical realm of the body. Unlike Offense, intense concentration and psychic strength were demanded by abilities such as [[Crucitorn (technique)|Crucitorn]], [[Hatred]], Horror, [[Memory Walk]], and [[Mind Shard]]<ref name="Book of Sith" />

====Sith magic====
{{Main|Sith sorcery/Legends}}
{{Quote|It is not sufficient to simply use Force powers, as the Jedi teach. Ritual gives spellcasting added power.|[[Sorzus Syn]], journal excerpt in ''[[Book of Sith]]''|<ref name="Book of Sith" />}}
The incantations of Sith magic were originated by the Sith [[Species/Legends|species]]. They included [[Sutta Chwituskak]] (Bolt of Hatred), [[Odojinya]] (Dark Side Web), [[Qâzoi Kyantuska]] (Suppress Thought), [[Dwomutsiqsa]] (Summon Demon), and [[Tsaiwinokka Hoyakut]] (Reanimated Dead).<ref name="Book of Sith" />

===Relativists and the Potentium===
{{Main|Potentium}}
Following an alternative philosophy regarding the Force, relativists argued that the dark side did not exist within the Force itself. They believed darkness was instead a manifestation of the individual Force-wielder's mind; since darkness was relative to the purity of their intentions, the use of dark side powers was justified if their intent was pure.<ref name="The Jedi Path" /> The [[Potentium]] philosophy and those who followed it held such beliefs, which both the Jedi Order<ref name="Jedi vs. Sith">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref> and the Sith regarded as a misguided and inaccurate view of the Force.<ref name="Darth Plagueis">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref> The name of the theory was also used by a group founded in [[132 BBY/Legends|132 BBY]] by [[Leor Hal]], who was expelled from the Jedi Order. Hal and his disciples taught that the Force, which they also called the Potentium, was inherently and inevitably good and without a dark side, and a being's connection with it should not be obscured through training or discipline.<ref name="Jedi vs. Sith" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Lukechoke2.png|thumb|right|250px|Luke Skywalker using Force Choke, a form of telekinesis.]]
[[West End Games]] originally established the Control, Sense, and Alter split for [[roleplaying game]] purposes in the first edition of [[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game (first edition)|''Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game'']]. As game mechanic, they functioned as three Force skills that a player character could train through skill points; without training, the skills could not be used. Force powers were methods of using one or more Force skills, with each power requiring a skill roll to determine its success or failure. For instance, "Contort/Escape" was a power governed by the Control skill, while "Projective Telepathy" required both Control and Sense. The rulebook emphasized that a power was not a "spell."<ref name="SW:TRG">[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game (first edition)|''Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game'']]</ref>

The [[2007]] ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Saga Edition Core Rulebook]]'' from [[Wizards of the Coast]] instead had a single Use the Force skill with Force Sensitivity and Force Training feats; Force powers were governed by Use the Force skill checks. Alter, Control, and Sense became Force talent trees rather than skills, alongside another talent tree for characters with Power of the Dark Side.<ref name="Saga">''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Saga Edition Core Rulebook]]''</ref> The reference book [[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']], written by [[Ryder Windham]] and published by [[Del Rey]] on [[November 27]], 2007,<ref name="Penguin: JvS">{{PenguinRandomHouse|url=books/192144/jedi-vs-sith-star-wars-the-essential-guide-to-the-force-by-ryder-windham/9780345493347|text=Jedi vs. Sith: Star Wars: The Essential Guide to the Force}}</ref> [[canon]]ized the names Control, Sense, and Alter as [[in-universe]] descriptions used to classify various uses of the Force rather than purely game mechanics.<ref name="Jedi vs. Sith" />
